name: Levenshtein edit distance
definition: The smallest number of single-character insertions, deletions, and substitutions that turn one string into the other, each costing 1. It is 0 only for equal strings, symmetric, and equal to the other string's length when one string is empty.
citations: Vladimir I. Levenshtein, Binary codes capable of correcting deletions, insertions, and reversals, Soviet Physics Doklady 10(8), 1966.
Gonzalo Navarro, A guided tour to approximate string matching, ACM Computing Surveys 33(1), 2001, section 2.

properties.says: The empty string to abc takes 3 insertions.
a to b is one substitution, costing 1.
A string is at distance 0 from itself.
Swapping the strings doesn't change the distance.

provenance.why: Chosen as a common numeric or text method from general knowledge, before any retained workspace was surveyed for candidates.
provenance.pattern: Check a well-known method against properties its standard definition implies (docs/coder/design/pattern-components.md, Fable step 6).
